findings.title: Symlink/`..` guard rejects valid output paths (macOS /tmp, relative `..` paths)
findings.message: Path.absolute() neither normalizes `..` nor resolves symlinks, so this check rejects any output path that merely *spelled* differently from its resolved form: `--output ../../consumers/out` run from inside the repo fails, and on macOS `--output /tmp/out` fails because `/tmp` -> `/private/tmp` is a system symlink. Only paths that actually resolve into the checkout are a safety problem; legitimate aliases like these are blocked, making the tool unusable for reasonable inputs.
findings.suggestion: Resolve first and test containment on the resolved path. A symlink pointing into the checkout still resolves under ROOT and is rejected, while harmless `..` components and system symlinks are accepted: `output = args.output.expanduser().resolve()` then `if output.is_relative_to(ROOT): raise ...`.

findings.title: Partial output directory is left behind when generation fails, blocking re-runs
findings.message: The output directory is created before extraction and generation run, but nothing removes it if a later step raises (check=True on new-app.py, the template-count check, or a manifest KeyError). Because mkdir is deliberately exclusive, every retry then dies with an unhandled FileExistsError until the operator deletes the half-populated directory by hand.
findings.suggestion: Wrap everything after the mkdir in try/except BaseException, remove the tree on failure (shutil.rmtree(output, ignore_errors=True)), and re-raise, so a failed run never burns the chosen output path. At minimum catch CalledProcessError and print which step failed.
findings.evidence:
output.mkdir(mode=0o700)  # exclusive; never replace existing source or notebooks
    sdk = checker.extract_verified(args.sdk, output/'sdk', verified)
    app = output/'Work Log'
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', str(sdk/'scripts/new-app.py'), str(app),
                    '--module=example.com/vellum-work-log', '--template=document'], check=True)

findings.title: Generated main.go is read and rewritten with locale-dependent encoding
findings.message: read_text()/write_text() use the locale-preferred encoding. On a C/POSIX-locale system any non-ASCII byte in the generated Go file raises UnicodeDecodeError, and on a cp1252 Windows system bytes are decoded and re-encoded with mojibake, silently corrupting the generated source.
findings.suggestion: Pass encoding='utf-8' to both read and write so generated Go source is round-tripped byte-safely regardless of locale.
findings.evidence:
text = main_go.read_text()
    old = 'Title: "Vellum Document"'
    if text.count(old) != 1:
        raise ValueError('SDK document template changed; review the Work Log customization')
    main_go.write_text(text.replace(old, 'Title: "Vellum Work Log"'))

fix.before:
main_go = app/'main.go'
    text = main_go.read_text()
    old = 'Title: "Vellum Document"'
    if text.count(old) != 1:
        raise ValueError('SDK document template changed; review the Work Log customization')
    main_go.write_text(text.replace(old, 'Title: "Vellum Work Log"'))
fix.after:
main_go = app/'main.go'
    text = main_go.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    old = 'Title: "Vellum Document"'
    if text.count(old) != 1:
        raise ValueError('SDK document template changed; review the Work Log customization')
    main_go.write_text(text.replace(old, 'Title: "Vellum Work Log"'), encoding='utf-8')
